quote: The Secretary of the Department of Finance and Administration shall increase annually the standard deduction ... by the cost-of-living adjustment for the current calendar year, rounding the amount to the nearest ten dollars ($10.00). ... not to exceed three percent (3%).
notes: Official Arkansas Code text is only on the LexisNexis-hosted site (not readable here); text read on FindLaw (current as of 2024-03-28, secondary). Subsection (b) sets the base at $2,200 per taxpayer from 2015; the later 2,340 -> 2,410 -> 2,470 path reported for 2023-2025 is consistent with (c). The 2025 bill HB1065 (arkleg.state.ar.us/assembly/2025/2025R/Bills/HB1065.pdf, engrossed) shows (c) in amended form and heading 'concerning the indexing of the standard income tax deduction to inflation', confirming indexing exists in present law (it would only remove the 3% cap and switch to the West South Central CPI). Enactment of HB1065 not checked. Cap and rounding come from FindLaw text of (c).

quote: (d) 'Adjusted individual credit' shall be twenty dollars ($20.00) ... (e)(1)(A) Not later than July 15 of each calendar year [the Secretary of Finance and Administration shall increase the credits by the cost-of-living adjustment] ... rounding each amount to the nearest dollar.

quote: The tables set forth in subdivisions (a)(1)-(3) of this section shall be adjusted annually in accordance with the method set forth in subsection (d) of this section.
section: Ark. Code 26-51-201(a)(4), (d)(1)-(2); the bracket adjustment ('recapture') is in (a)(1)(C), (a)(2)(C), (a)(3)(C)
notes: The recapture (bracket adjustment) range is part of the tables in (a)(1)-(3), which (a)(4) says are adjusted annually. Statute figures moved from 87,000 (2023) to 90,800 (2024 table), and the repo's 2025 start is 94,701, consistent with annual adjustment (the larger 2025 step also reflects the restructured 2024-25 tables). Official code not readable; FindLaw read. Confirm against the DFA's 2025 table if possible.

notes: SUSPENDED for 2025 and 2026: HB 96 (136th GA) uncodified Section 757.120(A): 'The Tax Commissioner shall not make adjustments in 2025 or 2026 to the income amounts in divisions (A)(2) and (3) of section 5747.02 of the Revised Code, as otherwise required by division (A)(5) of that section, or make adjustments in 2025 or 2026 to the personal exemption amounts prescribed in division (A) of section 5747.025 ...' (read at https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_136/legislation/hb96/07_EN/html). So the $26,050 and $100,000 starts hold flat through 2026 and the statute's indexing resumes for tax years from 2027 unless the legislature acts again. Note (A)(3)(c) for 2026 on has a single 2.75% rate above $26,050, so the $100,000 start ends after 2025. Earlier suspension for 2023-2024 also exists (secondary sources; not checked). The commissioner also never adjusts down.
